summary: Abraham Hyacinthe Anquetil-Duperron was a scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, Indology, and religious studies. He studied theology at the Sorbonne and Old Catholic Seminary of Amersfoort, and under Dastur Darab and Dastur Kaus. He held posts at the Bibliothèque nationale and Institut de France.

Abraham Richard Fuller was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as a Lieutenant in the Bengal Army (1849), Major in the Royal Artillery, and Director of the Department of Public Instruction, Punjab (1860–1867).

Abraham Sachs was a scholar of history, archaeology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Johns Hopkins University (ca. 1933–1937) and worked at the Institute for Advanced Study (1945) and Brown University (ca. 1948–1983).

Abraham Yohannan worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, religious studies, and linguistics. He studied at Columbia University under A. V. Williams Jackson from ca. 1895 to 1898 and held a post there from ca. 1895 to 1925.
Abraham Zablocki specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Cornell University and held a post at Agnes Scott College (attested 2008).
Acharya Buddharakkhita studied under Anton Walter Florus Gueth (ca. 1949–1952), Mahasi Sayadaw (ca. 1952–1954), and U Nārada. He also taught Laurence Khantipalo Mills.

Achim Bayer is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar. He earned his MA and PhD at the University of Hamburg under David P. Jackson and Lambert Schmithausen, later serving as a research associate at the University of Munich and fellow at Hamburg.

Achyutananda Dash is a scholar in Indology, philosophy, and linguistics. He was a Commonwealth Visiting Fellow at the University of Oxford (1997–1998) and held a post at Dr. Hari Singh Gour University (attested 1999).

Ada Maryla Falk worked in Indology and religious studies. She studied at the University of Florence under Paolo Emilio Pavolini and Sapienza University of Rome under Raffaele Pettazzoni, Carlo Formichi, and Giuseppe Tucci, later teaching at Rome and Calcutta.

Adalbert Bezzenberger studied linguistics and Indology at the University of Göttingen and University of Munich under Theodor Benfey and Martin Haug. He held posts at Göttingen and served as Professor of Sanskrit and IE at the University of Königsberg (1879–1921).

Adalbert J. Gail was an Indology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his doctoral studies under Helmut Hoffmann (ca. 1963–1968) and served at the Free University of Berlin from ca. 1978 to 2006.

Adalbert Kuhn was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He earned his PhD at Humboldt University of Berlin under Franz Bopp and Louis Poley, and served as a teacher, professor, and director at Cöllnisches Gymnasium between 1837 and 1870.

Adam Bowles specializes in Indology and religious studies. He earned his PhD at La Trobe University under Greg Bailey (1997–2004) and became Associate Professor in Asian Religions at the University of Queensland in 2009.

Adam Hardy specializes in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied architecture at the University of Cambridge and served as Professor of South Asian Art and Architecture at De Montfort University and Emeritus Professor at Cardiff University.

Adam Heinz was a linguist who studied at the University of Lviv under Jerzy Kuryłowicz and earned his PhD at Jagiellonian University under Jan Safarewicz. He held posts at the Pedagogical University of Krakow and Jagiellonian University.
Adam Hohenberger was an Indology and religious studies scholar. He studied under Ernst Windisch and earned his PhD from the University of Leipzig (1913–1918).

Adam Miller is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. He studied at Richland Community College, Western Illinois University, University of Missouri, and University of Chicago (PhD, 2014–2022). He has held adjunct teaching posts at Western Illinois, Heartland, Towson, and Mercyhurst.

Adam Pearcey is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD at SOAS University of London under Ulrich Pagel, Nathan W. Hill, and Vincent Tournier. He founded and serves as senior editor and translator at Lotsawa House.

Adam Yuet Chau is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies. He studied at Williams College and Stanford University (PhD, 1994–2001), completed a fellowship at Harvard University, and became Professor of the Anthropology of China at the University of Cambridge.
Adele Schlombs is a scholar in Sinology, history, and archaeology. She held posts at the Museum of East-Asian Art (1991) and the Museum für Ostasiatische Kunst Köln (ca. 1991–2022).
